audit.whatIsWrong: Four chart rows read 'Skill' in both layers where the packet and the page's own whys text both say Cassiopeia (Levels 1, 2, 6) or Sett (Level 3). The final rating line also said 'Hard matchup' while diff said EVEN and the tone was the hard-matchup red.
audit.why: whys[0] and whys[1] state Cassiopeia poke wins the first two levels, whys[2] calls Level 3 'your window', and whys[5] says Petrifying Gaze stuns your all-in at 6. Rendering 'Skill' over all four told the reader nothing and contradicted the sentence underneath.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Cassiopeia / Cassiopeia / Sett / Cassiopeia / Cassiopeia / Cassiopeia / Cassiopeia in both layers as one atomic paired group with ratings matched; report[14] and tone brought into line with EVEN.

audit.whatIsWrong: Miasma was the tracked ability on every panel with no cooldown given, and Twin Fang and Noxious Blast were described as 'ramping' with no numbers.
audit.why: Miasma is 24/22/20/18/16s — the longest cooldown in her kit and the whole reason a Level 3 window exists, since Facebreaker is 16s. Noxious Blast is 3.5s at 850 range and Twin Fang fires every 0.75s. Both ultimates are 120s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: 24s written into the cooldown panel, the do's, report[5] and phases[2]; the 16s-vs-24s comparison made the explicit reason Level 3 is yours; 3.5s and 0.75s written into the early phases; 120s into spikes[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: The page's headline interaction was that Miasma grounds you and 'dashes and movement abilities are disabled inside it'. Sett has no dash and no movement ability — the grounding does literally nothing to him. It also claimed 'Your R can suppress her', and never mentioned that Twin Fang heals her.
audit.why: Riot's Miasma text grounds and slows; against Sett only the slow is real, so the advice to track it for the grounding is advice about the wrong half of the ability. The Show Stopper's text is carry, slam, damage and landing slow — no suppression, and the mirror audit removed the identical claim. Twin Fang heals for a percentage of damage dealt, which is what actually beats Sett's Grit trades.
audit.corrected: Grounding demoted to the slow in the cooldown panel, the do's, report[5], spikes[2], spikes[3], whys[3], whys[6], late and wants.foe[0]; suppression removed from spikes[1]; Twin Fang's heal stated in dosFull[2].d and the anti-heal buy moved into report[8].

audit.whatIsWrong: First back was Phage / Tiamat against a champion who heals off every Twin Fang tick, and the item and TL;DR lines called Cassiopeia 'he' and 'his'.
audit.why: Twin Fang's heal is the reason extended trades go her way; Grievous Wounds is the item that changes that, not a Phage.
audit.corrected: First back changed to Executioner's Calling with the reason attached; pronouns fixed.

edits.before: Petrifying Gaze (R) stuns you if you face her -- she'll wait for your engage and hard-CC you mid-combo, then E Twin Fang you to death. Turn your back to break the stun into a slow, or bait R before committing. Your R can suppress her but her W slow makes reaching her the problem.
edits.after: Petrifying Gaze (R) stuns you if you face her -- she'll wait for your engage and hard-CC you mid-combo, then Twin Fang you to death. Turn your back to take the slow instead of the stun, or bait it out first; both ultimates are 120s at rank 1. Reaching her through Miasma is the real problem.

notes: The most useful correction here is a negative that had been sold as the matchup's core: the page's headline interaction was Miasma grounding Sett's dashes. Sett has no dash and no movement ability, so the grounding half of Miasma is inert against him and the slow is the entire threat. Everything downstream of that — when to step up, whether Flash actually helps, what 'bypassing the zone' means — was being taught off the wrong mechanic.
